data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:22 | [2024-08-24 17:44] derbymanager : - Fixed the bug that prevented players from retiring. - Youngsters will be generated only when the total number of non-retired players goes below 15000 (it's currently at 19000 so it might take a while to get new youngsters but I might force pull a few times to break the silence). - Renamed anticipation to creativity to better represent what it does. - Organised work rate, creativity, and focus to make it easier to remember what each of them does. Check wiki for details but basically work rate is for pressing and preventing build up (both short and direct), creativity for direct build up and attacking events (except shots), and focus for short build up, defensive actions, and all shots (as an attacker or goalkeeper). - Implemented momentum (or psychology or whatever you want to call it) that will increase losing team's build up power and decrease it for the winning team if the winning team has an early lead or leads by a lot. So, if your team is winning by a lot they will attack less while the opponent will attack more. Same goes if they score an early goal or two, they will naturally slow down a bit and the other team will take initiative. - How good your players are at getting back from behind depends on work rate and experience. How much will they slow down when they are in the lead depends on focus and experience (the lower their focus, the more they slow down). Note that only build up is affected, preventing build up is not affected by this. Note also that this kicks in exponentially so it barely makes any difference in close games. The intention is to give a bit of breathing room to a seriously weaker opponent. Basically, to make 5:0 results look like 3:1 perhaps, it won't make a difference between two equal teams playing 1:0 but it might help we get some surprise results. - Implemented home team advantage in the league, this time on purpose 😄 The boost is implemented on individual basis and depends on players' creativity and satisfaction (about 5-15% tops).
data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:24 | [2024-09-04 11:49] derbymanager : - Removed role familiarity, every player can play any role in a position they know. There will be some "preferences" for each player, e.g. one might prefer roles where you run a lot, while the other might prefer roles where you need to be intelligent or something like that, but for now the idea is for you to easily adapt to your opponents and, idk, play 541 if you're in over your head in d2 but quickly switch to a more offensive tactic (at least with roles) when you aim to win. - Also, just an explanation, sharpness grows faster with adaptability (part of experience), and drops slower with good potential or club fit, whichever is better. It's a small difference. In worst case two games will take a player from 0 to 44% sharpness, in best case to 51%. It takes 4 or 5 games in the row to get to green (80%+). Going down from 100% to 0% takes, in worst case scenario, 8 games, and in best case 12 games.

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:29 | [2024-09-22 15:12] derbymanager : **New roles** - Added a couple of new roles with the idea that M positions are what you would see as DM or M positions in FM, while F positions cover AM and F positions:  - Trequartista moved to FC positions  - Complete midfielder is in MC position instead  - Libero at DC that will move into DM position when the ball is high up the pitch  - Half winger on FLR positions that plays as inverted inverted forward 🙂 Basically, he is in the middle during build up but moves to the side in the final third (I know it would probably make more sense to have him in MC positions but this way every position has 4 roles)  - If you had tq in your squad, your formation is changed to have cm now. - All roles have been slightly changed, especially for direct build up (counters)  **Counters** - Direct build ups now work differently. Instead of there being a chance that a direct build up is selected, it is now tested when your team takes the ball from the opponents and brings it into the midfield. The steps are, more or less, like so:  - Opponent loses the ball and it gets carried outside of the danger zone  - The engine will first see if the counter is possible by comparing the number of your players against the opponent's remaining defence  - With short passing the counter will be attempted only if the numbers are more or less even, with direct passing your team might go for it even if it's 2 against 5. It also depends on how high is the ball.  - If the engine decides to try for counter, direct build up is tested to see if it succeeds or not.  - If that succeeds too, the action will resume and your team will continue play normally. Otherwise the action will stop.  - Left, centre, and right build up is now just regular build up used every time an action that is not counter starts. The starting scenario is generated closer to the centre with high press and similar options affecting it slightly.  **Other**

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:41 | [2024-10-28 09:37] derbymanager : **Big update this weekend**  ***Skills*** I made skills directly relate to events in the engine (for some events it's a combination of 2 skills, e.g. long pass consists of crossing + passing). The names are self explanatory I believe but here is an overview of what has changed:  - work rate => pressing (used to prevent build up) - anticipation => creativity (used to create build up) - ball control => crossing (for crosses, doh) - off the ball => first touch (used to receive passes) - focus => set pieces (for penalties, free kicks, corners...) - strength => aerial (for receiving crosses) - speed => agility (for running with ball but also avoiding offside and similar) - technique => dribbling (for dribbling, holding the ball etc) - accuracy => long shots (shooting from afar) - reaction => headers (putting crosses into the net)  In addition, pressure handling which is a part of experience is now called composure.  The rest stayed the same. Note that focus, work rate and anticipation are now just normal skills.  ***Other modifiers***
data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:42 | [2024-10-28 09:37] derbymanager : To keep things uncertain, because you only need one skill for most events now, the form, experience and other modifiers have been changed and also simplified:  1. Total value that is compared is skill + form modifier. Skill is at most 60 points, form modifier 40. That means a player with absolutely 0 skill can still have 40 points in an event simply from form. But... 2. How much of an impact form modifier has depends on club fit and experience. Together they move the lower limit form modifier can reach. But if either is very low, their impact is minimal and form swings will have higher impact. 3. In addition to form there are other modifiers that affect player's performance in a match:   - position familiarity (**up to** 25% penalty if playing in the same line, 50% if in another line, 75% if in goal).   - home modifier is up to 10% boost (depends on club fit).   - sharpness is up to 25% penalty.   - team spirit is up to 35% penalty.   - confidence replaces a lot of other smaller modifiers from before and is now a simple measure of player's level against the competition he is playing in. Professionalism prevents the player to become complacent too fast and composure to handle pressure well if he isn't good enough. Club fit also reduces this penalty. Up to 50% in theory, but in reality less than 10%.  ***Tactical options***
data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:46 | [2024-11-10 23:04] derbymanager : - Reworked how players mark others. The press value now has two numbers, how far up or down the pitch will the player move to mark someone, and the second number is how far left or right will he move to mark someone. This effectively creates a box that this player covers and he will mark players only within that box (relative to the position he should be in). E.g. limited defender has 3,9 which means he won't move far ahead to close down opponents but he will mark players that are far to the left or right of him. - Roam parameter works the same way. It is used for positioning attackers and players that have nobody to mark. - Condition will drop a bit lower but recovery is 3% per day. - Pressing tactical option increases how far ahead the player moves to press the opponent (makes the box that the player covers larger on x-axis). Condition consumption while playing pressing is increased (especially for players with low natural fitness). It also reduces counter chance as before (this didn't change just to be clear). - More passes will be considered long (the distance required to treat a pass as a long pass is shortened). - How close to the goal is the ball when the counter is tested matters a bit more now.

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:72 | [2025-04-24 06:58] derbymanager : *Just for clarification, you get a symmetry boost if you have a position on the left or left-centre side filled and that same position on the right side filled. So, XL + XR = boost. XLC + XRC = boost. XLC + XC => no boost. The role each player has is irrelevant, you get the boost as long as the position is filled.*  Also, having 3 players in the middle (e.g. MLC MC MRC) will also give boost as will having a solo FC (with or without FL and FR). Basically, all standard formations will give more or less equal boost so you don't have to optimize boosts. As long as your formation is symmetrical you'll get a maximum boost. For every player that is not symmetrical you miss out on a bit of a boost but it's not drastic enough to completely avoid ever playing assymetrical formations.

Overall, this didn't have a significant impact in games except in extreme cases. - I made players stand a bit wider or narrower depending on a formation. data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:86 | [2025-07-02 16:25] derbymanager : -----  **Training**  The idea behind the old training was that bad facilities mean you can still train players but you have less versatility when it comes to what you can train, while good facilities remove that limitation. This has made a lot of people very angry and been widely regarded as a bad move. So I made a few adjustments, but the general premise is the same: players train best when they play in a team that is above their tier.  - Your team's tier and player's potential and club fit set the maximum level he can reach. - Then there are variables that affect player's chance for a skill pop:   - 1st variable: Three training facilities each affect their own set of skills and define at what skill level player trains best the best. For example, facilities at level 7 will have the highest chance when training players with skill 7. The chance slowly drops so even with facilities at 1 there is a chance to increase the skill to 20, although this chance is lower than with better facilities.   - 2nd variable: Players with 2-4 stars will usually train the best. For low tier teams the peak can be even at 5 stars, but normally it's lower. The exact "peak stars" depends on player's club fit.   - 3rd variable: Player's peak training happens somewhere between their age of 18 and 25.   - 4th variable: Sharpness works as before. Sharpness of 0 means no training, sharpness at 100% means the maximum you can get from the first 3 variables.   But that's not all!   - To align with the new skill/training system, mentors provide fewer mentor points but as you can see they're even more important now. - Which skills belong to which training category has been changed (and makes more sense now IMO). - And most importantly, the skill you focus on has a small fixed chance to grow at all times (assuming the player and skill can grow at all). That means it can grow even for players that don't play and oldies. Normal training modifiers are added on top on this fixed base.

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:130 | [2026-10-21 22:44] derbymanager : **Mid-late season 26 update**  - Substitutions. No, seriously. You can now set 5 players on the bench. Subs will happen around the 60th minute and on injuries or red cards of course. In the set pieces view you can also set who they should replace:   - Sub low condition player in your position   - Sub low performing player in your position   - Sub only when the match is already decided (winning or losing by 2) - for development purposes   - Sub no matter what   - Auto: assistant decides (mix of low condition, yellows & bad performance) - Yes, that means that injuries and cards happen during the game, not at the end. - Form is back, but simplified. It's not revolving constantly up and down over a period of time anymore. Instead, it goes up when playing a match and down when not playing a match (for whatever reason). How fast it is going up varies, and every time the player skips a match the speed it's going up changes. So, pushing your fast-growing players to play as much as possible is preferable, but of course that increases the risk of injuries so your mileage may vary. - Build up has changed. I spent too much time to create this dot-matrix of which positions can pair together to push towards realistic formations without preventing you to play whatever you want (if you don't mind losing a bit of build up). It works like this: There are 13 dots, 5 for pressing and 8 for regular build up. Each dot needs two players to be filled. Those players must be in specific direction from the dot. Since there are only so many dots, having too many players around a single dot means they all can't contribute and you may end up with fewer than 10 dots, effectively cutting yourself short by 10% build up for each missing dot... - Report bugs so I can fix them and leave the engine alone next season 🙂

The game was showing you the injury chance, which is a combination of condition and form. But that was confusing so now it's showing condition only and exact injury chance is not visible.  Injury chance was a bit too high so I reduced it.  Changed how subs work a bit. You can set player's match status for any player (pitch or bench) like so:  Gets in: - RAT: Replaces a player in his position that has a rating 0.5 or more lower than the average of his team - CON: Replaces a player in his position that has condition below 80% - AUTO: Only gets in when he fits someone else's get out requirement (he is the right position) - DEV: Gets in only when the score is +/-2, combining rating and condition who to replace - IMP: Gets in as a priority if the team isn't winning - EMR: Only gets in on an injury  Gets out: - RAT: If he has a rating 0.5 or more lower than the average of his team or lower than 6.5 if anyone on the bench can replace him. - CON: If he has less than 80% condition if anyone on the bench can replace him - AUTO: combines rating and condition - DEV: Gets out as a prioirty when the team isn't winning. When winning he is treated as auto. - IMP: Can get out only if winning by two goals, in which case he is treated as auto. - EMR: Not a part of planned changes, only gets out on an injury  Yellow cards add a bit of weight to all of these. Subs always happen between 55-65 minutes (and a 3rd around 110 if it comes to that).  Player's training requirement behaves like this: - it goes down by 1 if he plays at least 20 minutes - it goes down by 2 if he played at least 45 minutes - it goes back to 1 no matter where it was if he played 75 minutes or more  Build up now warns you when there is an overflow of players in some area or when there are too few players in a critical area. Each warning reduces your build up.  And adjustments to the engine so defenders hold the line better, players don't tire so much from running, etc.

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:1304 | [2023-05-25 13:39] derbymanager : Both are in game, the logic behind who knows is a bit different.  - Current way, news travel through your country and your direct competitors can find out about your target. Someone might check that player and decide to go for him. There is real risk involved in going public because not-interested people might get interested. But also, you might miss interested people. Even from your country, a manager might simply miss the news.  - Your way, there are no news (I can't target individual managers) but whoever spends 2 scouts sees it. It's safe to assume, since you have nothing to lose, that everyone interested will spend two scouts before buying. So everyone interested will see it. The only difference is that you won't gather extra interest (which is the fun part).  When you know that there is some interest your best approach is to go with 3rd scout as well. Not that you can't catch the player with 2 scouts only, but your chances will be better with 3 scouts. There is a bit of decision making if there is only one interested team, you might want to sneak up on that team. But in that case:  - Current way, you can't be sure if there is more than one interested team. You have to assume there are more. But the first team, the one already interested, can try to sneak in a low offer because: a) maybe nobody joins the bidding war, and b) even if they see the news they might think it's already too late as maybe more than one team is bidding... It's harder to make decision if you don't have complete information.  - Your way, you know exactly that there is only one interested team and that you have to offer more. Since that interested team can also check if someone else joined knows that you can 100% see that they're interested - they shouldn't make a weak offer. So this approach falls apart. It actually puts the team with 3rd scout at a very vulnerable position and benefits everyone else... So, don't use 3rd scout.

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:3453 | [2023-07-10 09:59] derbymanager : Anyway, it's all connected so this is my plan for this week:  A.) Engine. Players should cover less space, maybe I will prevent them from running 2 zones in a row or there will be even bigger chance they won't run due to low work rate.  B.) Budget > I think we can easily transpose DM1 and change the day by day income by matches and revenues with fixed semester income performance based It already basically works like this. Your team earns money per season and that's the base for your budget. Money you save is transferred for the next window. If you save a lot of it then the board will take something. I.e. if you have 18M the board could take 3M and give you 15M on top of what you normally get.  What I was thinking is making budget based on windows, not seasons. So you get a new budget every window but it's smaller. Salaries would also be paid by window...  C.) Training. Currently there are no skill drops and some skills are worth more than others. For example, finishing was imagined as a mental skill that could shift quickly from 17 to 13 for example. The player had something happen in private life and his confidence dropped, so you can see his finishing going down. The expectations, however, are that skills are quite static and growing with training, especially for youngsters. Seeing your 19yo lose 4 points of finishing makes people rage quit (off topic, but getting +4 on one skill never makes anyone rage join 🤔 )...  So, what I plan to do is make all behave the same and making determination, work rate, and focus more important. You want a clinical striker, get one with high determination and good skills. The skills will be split into 2 categories, one that moves super slow but don't drop with age, and other that rely on age more and are more likely to drop.  D.) Prices. Current prices are based on tier. Basically, all players are sorted in descending order and the prices follow that order. I will base it directly on skills in the future no matter their position.

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:3524 | [2023-07-10 15:40] derbymanager : But anyway, the idea is that FDW affect something more than regular skills and to keep them all high should be really hard for all players.  Focus - ME: passing actions + penalties + fouls + offsides and other small "mistakes" - non ME: affects satisfaction (i.e. the player is partying and it hurts team spirit) - Behaves: grows faster when trained, drops faster when not playing, drops slowly when not training (depends on xp-pressure)  Determination - ME: saves and shots,  - non ME: fewer skill drops (determined players last longer, which is often the case for gks and forwards), a bit better training - Behaves: chance to change during transfer windows, will certainly change when changing clubs (depending on xp-adaptability)  Work rate - ME: movement actions, can "refuse" to move into position if he's tired - non ME: affects the condition loss and fitness indirectly - Behaves: can be trained above the natural tendency but it'll drop back when training stops, depends on age and xp-professionalism

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:7312 | [2023-10-31 11:35] the.painkiller : - The pitch is divided in 15 squares from A1 to C5 - Positions are divided into D, M and A - Every square has a value of predefined event skill (like in DM1 with BU, PBU etc) given by the skills of every player that contributes for that single square - Single player's contribution to each square is modified by his role, so a MLC-Mezzala will shift 20% from B3 to A3, MC-Holding Midfielder will shift 20% from B3 to B2 etc - The ME picks the ball as the trigger of each square event, so for example in case of a goal kick the square is B1, and depending on the tactical options you can choose to let the ME pick one event or another; continuing the goal kick example, if you set up for direct play, you trigger more the event long pass and so LPvsPLP, if succesfull the ball moves ahead to B3 (or A3 or C3 depending of exploit the middle/sides), if you set up for possession you trigger BUvsPBU, if succesfull the ball moves to B2, or A2/C2 - The ME calculates beforehand the whole action until there's a shot and, in case of high xG the live view shows it no matter if it ends in a goal, a save or a shot off the goal - Regarding the point above, I'd go totally live view-less, just pure commentary so to avoid any headache about making the live view be realistic or such - Mandatory in case of total live view-less but necessary even in case of live view, real time stats: ball possession, shots, tackles, each player's rating

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:7997 | [2024-06-15 23:05] derbymanager : I don't know what you think I'm coping with... Anyway, I'm on the way to bed now so I'll try to summarize. The way I'm using form now allows me to have variance between players. Having form just be another X% modifier on everything is one dimensional. I could merge it with condition so that you don't have to calculate it yourself. Having it treated as another skill (combined with focus and anticipation) lets me have multiple dimensions instead of one. For example, your player might have good skills that negate his bad form, while with a flat modifier to everything his skills also get negated.  Let's say that for "fake pass" action the formula is passing * 3 + ball control + form. And let's say the calculation for form is 50%. Current way still allows the player with passing 20 to be really really good at fake pass and get 60 points from it, while a flat modifier would make that 30 points from passing completely ruining that player.  Sure, 50% is too much of an impact, but a flat modifier will never be the right amount because 25% of 100 is 25, which is a significant amount, but 25% out 20 is 5, which is insignificant. Basically, the better the player, the more important form becomes.  So, my suggestion is to simply treat form as another skill because, honestly, it's not that far from being just that. I mean, you don't concern yourself with exact impact of any other skill...
data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:7998 | [2024-06-16 10:29] derbymanager : So, since some others also pinged me about this form thing and since I want to keep things transparent but not reveal any formulas behind the game I'll try to explain it with an example.  In a formula for a single action, form is used like any other skill in a sense it has absolute value, it isn't a modifier that multiplies anything.  Unlike other skills, form is used in all actions thus it is very important. But it is also combined with FAW so you should look at all of them together.  The importance comes from being used everywhere, but how much it is important varies with your play style. For example:  There are 50 passes per match so passing will be used 50 times. Formula for passing puts more emphasis on passing than on form alone (let's say 2x) so, overall, that's 100 * passing and 50 * form. These are just arbitrary numbers for this example, they're not real numbers used in the game.  But form affects shooting as well, while passing doesn't. However, there are only 10 shots per game. Again, finishing is more important, let's say 3x so finishing * 30 and form * 10.  Total for form is 50 + 10 (+ whatever values are there for all other actions, but let's keep it simple and have only 2 actions for this example). That's, overall, less than passing (100) and more than finishing (30). But if there are 20 shots in your game and 25 passes the numbers are now 50 for passing, 60 for finishing, and 45 for form. That's why I can't give you an exact percentage, because it depends on what happens in the match.  Personally, I treat form the same as I treat Focus for example. I take it into account but I don't consider it crucial. More often than not my squad is determined simply by who is available for a specific position with the goal to increase training for younger players. Form is one of the things that helps me decide, it's not crucial.

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:9651 | [2024-08-25 17:07] derbymanager : Situations that could happen with sharpness that can't happen now: - Your key player gets back from the injury before the important game. He has high condition, low sharpness... The one who replaced him has medium condition and high sharpness. Who do you play? - Your reserve DC is getting low on sharpness but your primary DC still has good condition. Do you switch them now so you have a solid replacement on your hands or do you risk not having a good replacement when you need him. - One player has medium condition and high sharpness, the other one high condition and low sharpness... The first one is in poor form and has 4 stars, the second one is in great form and has 3 stars. Which one do you pick? - Your first 11 has several players with low condition and the rest are moderate or good condition. They're all at good sharpness since you didn't rotate much. If you replace them all, the benefit is minor because of the lost sharpness, so there is no incentive to do it all at once. Better to keep 2 more players with high sharpness so you can make a few rotations every match and keep all 13 at optimal range... - You have a couple of youngsters that you want to give some training. Do you try to give them all a bit of playtime and small chance to grow, or do you force just two of them and give them more training? Right now you can't pump up training by playing more than 2 games in a row because you hit the upper limit of training effort and it'll all be gone in 3 days...

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:11147 | [2024-09-27 15:44] derbymanager : No hard feelings, it's just that when these role discussions are brought up it's always about names but nobody gives concrete ideas what to change. There are 5 "ball" positions and 5 "player" positions, so basically 25 combinations for movement. And a lot of those combinations are not viable or are too similar to each other. The whole match engine is in the wiki, I'm not hiding 60 developers in my basement to create 100 decisions per minute per player match engine that FM has... The MC position has a lot of versatility as it moves across 3 different lines. This gives you 5 different combinations: - DM - DM / M - DM / M / AM - M / AM - AM The first 4 are on the MC position and pure AM that doesn't drop behind is TQ which is on FC position. There is literally nothing more to add except to change that *this* DM/M moves to M when the ball is at centre, while *that* DM/M moves to M when the ball is in attack only... Which is a minor timing adjustment.  Compare that to defenders that all stand on the D line, except libero (which is a half back but I didn't want to crowd the MC position with it as well) and forwards that, without TQ and F9, would be equally limited in where they move. TM and CF move exactly the same (I tried to differentiate them with preferences), no sense in adding one more forward position that does the same.  As for side players, you get extra movement options when they cut inside. That's one role (or two in case of forwards). There is also some overlap in movement to allow for formations like 352 with DWGs or 532 with AWBs, but these players often cover more space than central positions so it's easier to create more roles. For example, FB stays back always, WB moves up but not all the way, AWB moves all the way up, and IWB moves into the middle. That's 4 highly distinctive roles.

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:11863 | [2024-11-25 20:03] yasen_gg : I've been busy all day, so could barely respond. But the point I wanted to make is that there are multiple factors that need to align for you to get anything out of the training:  - You need to have at least one player with good potential and at the right time of development for him to start gaining very fast - Even if you lack the player that will explode in development, you still need 3-5 players in that group (Def/Mid/Fwd)   - If you train just for one person, you are throwing efficiency away - You need to actively manage to switch skills - You need to have the right facilities to make sure the skill you can train can even be trained to max level - You also need to make sure your player does not peak along the way or start requiring better facilities  And even when you do all the things right and finally get a skill to 20 - trust me you will not see the difference between marking 20 and marking 15 defenders. Apart from FCs and GKs who's efficiency you can directly evaluate in goals scored/conceded - you'll only see progress with the improvement of your team as a whole.  TLDR - for me, training is neither too fast, nor OP - you just get to have great periods, especially if you focus on having a squad full of youngsters.

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:13484 | [2025-02-19 08:57] derbymanager : So, I'll use this opportunity to announce the change I'm planning. Because even though I argued the numbers work here, I'm not happy with the solution where midfielders create and defenders prevent it as it is now. The real issue is that overloading attack seems to be working really well and we see formations like 235 generating large xg but suffering very little.  One reason is definitely that players aren't good on counter, which is something I'm working on too.  But another reason is that creating chances is better than preventing them. If you play 5-4-1 it'll be hard to clear the ball out of your defence and stop the attack. Instead, your defender will clear the ball, their defender will pick it up and send it into your half again and that same attack continues.  So, the end result is that if the bot plays 451 for example, you can nullify it with 1 defender basically and overload their 4 at the back with 5 attacking players, leaving someone free to shoot on each attack...  There is no option to simulate 90% of the match that is just passing the ball around like so: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Wcvo3F-SeFk so the build up mechanic is used to abstract that part.
data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:13485 | [2025-02-19 09:05] derbymanager : Another thing that bothers me (and salty and many others probably) is that when a counter starts there is a check if you successfully created a counter, which happens after your player already got the ball. So a clear action that's flagged as counter opportunity can get shut down through this build up mechanic. So I'd like to remove that and replace it with build up from defence.  There would then be 4 different build ups, defence + left/central/right and your team would have to first succeed on building from defence, then one of the l/c/r build ups would get triggered, and if you succeed on that one too -> you see the action.  Defenders would then build from defence mostly, midfielders would build up l/c/r and also prevent l/c/r build up, and forwards would press and prevent build up from defence. Different roles would mix those assumptions.  This would also make pressing tactical option more important as it could reduce opponent's build up if you use it.
data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:13486 | [2025-02-19 09:07] derbymanager : More or less the change comes down to:  - 2 checks to create an action, more areas to focus play on. - what is now role's direct build up contribution becomes defensive build up contribution (with some smaller adjustments probably).

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:14467 | [2025-05-05 09:45] derbymanager : Counters are based on the ratio of defenders and attackers in front of the ball (which might be like half of the field). So, if you play short passes then there needs to be cca. the same number of your own players in front of the ball (including the one with the ball) as there are defenders. E.g. 4 on 4 is a counter, but 3 on 4 isn't. It's a bit more complex, it takes into account where the ball is (e.g. if you're already close to the goal 3 on 4 might also be a counter with short passing)... Playing counters means you will try it evein if it's 1 against 4.  Basically, when your team regains possession there is a check if it should be a counter as explained above, and if not there is a check to see if you manage to create a build up with those 2 build up steps. If it's a counter you bypass the build up step so that's good, but the whole situation is not in your control. Your AWB might be too far behind or the formation could be completely shuffled... If it's not a counter you have the build up phase to deal with instead (which you might fail) but your formation is adhered to.   Playing counters therefore starts from a more chaotic situation and it can happen that you lose the ball with the first pass you make... Build up starts with more organised situation and will usually give the player with the ball some solid options what to do with the ball. If you're the better team this is probably the better approach.

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:14939 | [2025-05-16 07:04] derbymanager : It's actually working quite close to how it is intended. It just doesn't make it easy to hyper-optimise, which is by design. We're not playing factorio. All I hear are complaints from people that want to have only 16 youngsters in their squads and play an investment brokers with their teams...  But, the idea is to have 4 groups of players: - 5 oldies, they are losing value but are at least ok backup players and provide more or less mentoring. - 5 peak players, ages 25-30, they are not growing much but bring you results. Some of them will start having mentoring points and you can decide to keep them when they turn into oldies. - 5 youngsters, these are the useful players that are still growing. They will either reach their peak and go into the group above, or they will become unhappy and want to move to a different team where they maybe can grow more. - 5 school players, they may or may not get enough playtime to train, few of them will go into the group above, the rest will get sold or released.  All complaints are that having 15 youngsters, few peak players and 0 oldies is problematic. And I think that's how it's supposed to be. You want 15 youngsters, then be ready to rotate them when they get to red training. Or get some fucking mentors. You can have different distributions of the above, like 4/10/2/4 instead of 5/5/5/5 and it should work. But I don't care that 0/20/0/0 has issues. It's your choice to go for that. The squad building part of the game is finding the ratio that works well for your team and adjusting on the fly. Not just programatically buying mentoring points for cheap, youngsters that will 100% double their price in 3 seasons (and never become unhappy), and playing the current meta formations... I will always fight against that.

Allowing managers to pick the role a player has on the field will allow that flexibility. - The B team has no purpose right now. I would have kept them as youth teams where each team were supposed to have a 11 players that form a proper lineup, not just 7 GK and 3 DR. Youth teams had a charm, and were a feature that could have been expanded. As of right now the B team (especially for bots) is an extension of the first team with a different training regime. - Youth intake (one of the best feature in FM) is a complete miss in DM. No one knows when it happens, no one knows what to expect and when you get a youth player, the feeling is almost always anticlimactic. Motorsport Manager 3 has a fantastic youth program feature that gets you involved with your youths way before you get to know what their potential is and allows you to influence them before their final ability is revealed to you. - Training should be changed in a way that allows the player to influence the players, while at the same time keeping the existing random stats improvement that differentiate players between one another.
data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part2.txt:5878 | [2019-12-10 23:16] derbymanager : 1.) Roles. Previously, players were fixed. They played in 1-3 roles and that was it. You wanted ML to play as AML - tough luck. Now you can set him as winger and he will cover 3 wing positions. I assume the confusion comes from white and empty circles - what you see now (both white and empty) would previously correspond only to white circles in terms of proficiency (white was previously up to 10% penalty, same as empty now).  It is true that you could switch roles easier, assuming the player supported them. But this change was partially inspired by something you said salty - that tactic doesn't play part when playing against other managers as you can't predict what they will play so it's impossible to counter them. The new system should help with that as it is easier to assess what your opponent has available and how he can modify his tactic. This is the reason why it takes a couple of days to switch player's role so that your opponent couldn't surprise you.  But the main reason I made the switch is because now I can easily add new roles to players (there are currently 75 combinations compared to 40 that were before) and it should make training directly connected to what happens on the field. I'll come back to training later but I wanted to connect training with the game instead of having just some add-on that improves price no matter what you choose.

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part2.txt:7212 | [2020-01-30 07:09] saltylem0n_ : **Assistant manager** takes care of squad's physical skills and helps them recover from injuries faster. He gives up to +4% per star bonus to both injury recovery and training speed for physical skills (speed, strength, work rate and set pieces).  **Technical coach** is responsible for training technical skills of your players. He increases the training speed by up to +4% per star for technical skills: tackling, accuracy, passing, technique, finishing, handling.  **Tactical coach** handles the training of tactical skills. Like others, he also increases the training speed by up to +4% per star for: ball control, anticipation, positioning, vision, off the ball and marking skills.  **Business manager** handles finances and increases the revenue from sponsors. His effort depends on your facilities level and will bring up to 60000 money per star. Use business manager if you want stable and reliable income per day.  **Brand specialist** takes care of club's brand recognition. He increases home match attendance (up to 4000 per star) and merchandise revenue (up to 40000 per star), both of which depend on fans' satisfaction. If your fans are happy and your teamwork is high, you might want to consider using brand specialists instead of business managers. While merchandise income on itself is lower than sponsors, increased income from attendance can easily offset the total revenue in brand specialist's favour.  **Scout** can bring youth players into your club and help you identify scouting targets. He increases the potential and initial power of your youths and the rate at which your club generates them, all by up to 4% per star. He will also increase the rate at which you regenerate scout reports by the same amount and help you a bit to find potential transfer targets.

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part2.txt:9827 | [2020-05-06 18:33] derbymanager : Every staff member has a role in terms of game mechanics:  BM is the benchmark staff, he should give stable income without any risk or requirements, but he should also be outperformed by other staff members if some requirements are satisfied. BS is the first example, if you have good team spirit he should bring you a bit more money. If you, in addition, focus on buying charismatic players he should be much better. This one is quite predictable actually and you can mathematically calculate whether he's better than BM or not (which isn't something I like, I want all other functions to have a level of risk but ok). TC and TC should be beneficial if you focus on youngsters, especially if they have some traits that improve training speed, and if you support them with mentors. These require a lot of effort as you have to get the right players (both young and old) and suffer team spirit penalty while trading them (since you don't generate money). It is risky because there are many variables involved but the risk isn't all or nothing, maybe if you don't do it right you'll lose 10% or 20% of potential money you could have got from BM. AM is lesser TC or TC because he trains only 4 skills instead of 6, but in return your injuries get recovered faster. So he's a bit riskier than other coaches in terms of money earned but helps with injuries which can be significant in terms of performance and winning leagues. It's hard to put money value on that.

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part2.txt:11970 | [2020-08-18 08:37] derbymanager : Add to that that you don't control default training and that training, more or less, has a limit. Let's simplify and say that, with his potential and all, your player can gain +5 before he simply can't grow anymore. He's 26 and has 4.5 stars or whatever. You can give him default training and he'll grow by +5 in 4 skills in the next month. Or you can focus him on accuracy and get +5 there in the next month and a half. Do you take a bit more time to get the player you need, or do you go with whatever is in the box?  Which brings me to the main reason for the change - newcomers and <@!404638465851129857> don't know which skills are important and how the game really works. It's a bit of a black box for them and they rely on intuition. If they want an easier game and don't want to learn how everything works - they can just leave training on default for the most part and won't miss a lot.  I had several people ask me about training and it's really easy to give them a solution now: default is good enough, focus is if/when you want to experiment, but you're not obliged to do so to stay competitive.

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part3.txt:9288 | [2024-05-10 17:05] .jarles : _ _ 4. Position and roles: Player learns roles as he plays them. It takes from 5 to few dozen games to learn a role to 100% (depending on player's adaptability). If the player doesn't know how to play a role he might get up to 20% penalty on his performance if he plays in the right position. E.g. a MC that has BTB role plays as TQ will suffer up to 20% penalty on his first game but will quickly learn the new role. If the player is playing in the same line (e.g. DC as DL) the maximum penalty increases to 40%, if he plays on the same side (e.g. ML as FL) the penalty is up to 60%, and if he plays at completely different position the penalty is close to 80%. Players with better experience (specifically Adaptability) will suffer lower penalty and learn new role/position faster.   Feedback: These penalty numbers seems a bit absurd. data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part3.txt:9437 | [2024-06-03 13:50] derbymanager : Here is from the wiki:  Form affects other stats (e.g. focus, anticipation) and cyclically rises and falls. When high, it will start to decrease, and when low, it will start to increase. Exact points it'll change direction depend on club fit and chance.  If form is growing, playing matches increases the chance it'll start falling. This chance is higher when form is higher.  When form is falling, playing matches decreases the chance it'll turn around. This chance is higher when form is lower.

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part3.txt:15202 | [2025-06-28 22:56] furysk : I've seen several systems out there that games use.    FM, hockey-nation, and hardwood base their players development on having decent enough coaches to get the player there quickly, but their top end builds are set in stone.  Hardwood similar to this game allows for a slight boost in focus on a specific area, but it's more like a 10-15% boost to that one area while the player still develops everywhere.  Hockey-nation is basically a single minimum and 2 maximums are known, and you have to decide the skills/overall a player can get based on where those have capped yet if any, and you more specifically set the development on a player by player basis.  FM has a bit of a mix of the two and is the most complicated as it introduces other metrics to the equation.  There are other systems, a game such as buzzer beater (basketball sim) thats been around for a long time has players that are not set in stone at all, but their potential determines their semi-hard cap (they can still with tons of extra time skill up, but it's about a 5-10% development rate), and it's set by position, so you can gain slightly more total skill if you balance a players training, or you can make them more specialists, but all is dependant on their potential at the end of the way.

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part3.txt:15297 | [2025-06-29 17:07] derbymanager : I agree training (and everything) could be better explained for new owners but that's not my goal at this point, I'm mostly focused on making things work well enough first. The game goes through many changes until I find what works, sometimes small adjustments have a butterfly effect across the game, and changing wiki again and again isn't fun for me.  That being said, I don't know what's there to not understand about training.  You basically have 3.5 variables: - your facilities (F) - player potential (P) - club fit, age and some other variables like age (C) - sharpness, not a variable like the others because you have full control over it (S)  And the formula is something like: P * (F + C) All numbers being better gives you the higher final result.  Then sharpness sets the percentage of that number you get as a training chance. If sharpness is 0, the player isn't training. If it's at 100%, the player is training as good as he can considering those 3 variables.

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part4.txt:2711 | [2025-07-31 09:56] derbymanager : The game is changing pretty fast as it's still in beta while I try to balance it all... The best approach is to simply ask here on discord and people will help you out.  From the design perspective, the goal is to reward having a balanced team, a mixture of mentors, youth prospects and everything in between. Whenever there is a perceived meta I try to nerf it so that it isn't the best (or only) way to play. Even if one approach is perhaps too good at the moment, you can count on it getting worse in the future.  In terms of how to play, my suggestion would be: - Analyse your team, make sure you have good players all around for the formation you intend to play (it's enough to just look at the stars in the squad selection screen). Don't shy away from playing players out of position, they'll learn the new position and will play well there in 5-10 games. - Generally speaking, 1 or 2 bad players in your squad won't break you. You can play a formation that you know works well and fill a position or two with 500k youngster if needed. Of course, better players usually mean better results, but that's not guaranteed and prepare that you'll get angry at match engine occasionally 😬 - If you need money you can sell one good player and buy two ok ones. For example, you sell Valle and buy two 5-8M players to fill up your squad with 3.5 star players. You have a lot of youngsters, maybe offload those you don't intend to play and buy another 5-8M player. Selling shitty players might be tough, though. - Your main goal should be to go up to 3rd division. Don't worry about player development, facilities, or anything else. I would buy older (25+) quality players that will push you up. The rewards basically double with each division so you want to get as high as possible as fast as you can.

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part4.txt:2995 | [2025-08-08 15:36] poletz : Each role has a different contribution to defensive build up, build up, prevent defensive build up and prevent build up.  This number is multiplied for his ability in each of those 4. U can see skills involved in one of the last updates.  So all players contribution in each phase are summed and u ve the value u see in the post match report.  Es: def bu : 49/27 (64%) The math is 49/(49+27) = 64%  It means that 64% of ur def bu attempts will be succesful Hence the other number u ve there : 32/51. Is not exactly 64% cause there are other little modifiers but more or less it s this.  Same for all the others .  If u attack from right to left your numbers are those on the right, and viceversa for the other side.  Numbers of def bu actions attempted are always around 50/60. Some of them are turned to counters according to settings and lineups. So it can became lower, imagine 45. Then of this 45 the succesful can be 30. Then this 30 is splitted among left/center/right bu. Those are ur attempts to bu there and also there same math to se how many are succesfull. These will be your action (and add counters to this)  Hope this can help. Told this u can play ignoring bu, it s not so important 🙂

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part4.txt:3238 | [2025-08-27 23:29] furysk : from recent experience as someone in IV who was 7-10-20 in their first 37 and 27-6-6 in the last 39, the things that made it work for me after a while:  1) Do not build to a formation that works for someone else.  they have the players to make it work, you probably dont, so just build your team based on what you have to work with early on.  The only formations that tend not to work as easily (though still doable) are ones that aren't somewhat symmetrical. Experience is great, but if you can find the right guy that is 22-25 and is near the end of development, make them your tier 4 cornerstone and hope they accept a backup contract down the road or they can be sold to be someone elses tier 4 winning player. data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part4.txt:16507 | [2024-08-27 10:52] derbymanager : Anyway, there are several cases in DM: 1.) two equally good teams, eg. salty vs poletz 2.) one team much better than the other, e.g. cup game 3.) two equally good teams but one is fielding dc as fc or gk and has trouble bringing out the correct team  with current xg: 1.) you know who did tactically better, and I think that's the most important thing anyone wants to know. 2.) your xg is higher than it should be because the other team is weaker. Does it matter if you won 3:0 with 3xg or 1.5xg? In real life it would show 1.5xg and it would look like you overperformed xg. Since you only see 1.5xg and you don't know that the "real" xg was 3 you can only guess the impact the difference in power had. 3.) you have to check why you had high xg and probably, since you know you fielded your best team, the reason is the gk or defenders.  with real world xg: 1.) player abilities don't matter so you don't know who did tactically better, we can only guess 2.) xg is 1.5 but you scored 3. how much was gk responsible for that? who knows 3.) the two teams might have similar xg, so you can't tell how much of an impact the wrong players had and how much it was luck  Basically, for adjusted xg you have two variables, ability and luck that you have to guess and there is no way to know exactly how much of an impact they had. With current xg you have only one variable, ability, and you can calculate luck.

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part4.txt:17281 | [2024-09-03 08:25] poletz : - Implemented momentum (or psychology or whatever you want to call it) that will increase losing team's build up power and decrease it for the winning team if the winning team has an early lead or leads by a lot. So, if your team is winning by a lot they will attack less while the opponent will attack more. Same goes if they score an early goal or two, they will naturally slow down a bit and the other team will take initiative. - How good your players are at getting back from behind depends on work rate and experience. How much will they slow down when they are in the lead depends on focus and experience (the lower their focus, the more they slow down). Note that only build up is affected, preventing build up is not affected by this. Note also that this kicks in exponentially so it barely makes any difference in close games. The intention is to give a bit of breathing room to a seriously weaker opponent. Basically, to make 5:0 results look like 3:1 perhaps, it won't make a difference between two equal teams playing 1:0 but it might help we get some surprise results.

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part5.txt:14677 | [2025-08-22 21:33] yasen_gg : My rough ideas are:  - Playing a game consumes condition in real time - Performance depends on condition during the game - Fitness affects condition loss during the game - Injury chance increases as condition goes lower - Players can get both knocks and injuries    - Knocks lower condition after the end of the game (but player can play)    - Injuries make the player unavailable for selection - Sharpness affects starting condition - Condition recovery depends on facilities    - Low level facilities (D4-D3) provide post-game recovery allowing you to play 1 game per day easily.    - Mid level facilities (D2-D1) allow you to play 2 games per day here and there    - Top level facilities (Elite+) allow you to play 2 games per day consistently   This way: - Teams will be able to play their best teams more regularly relative to their club level - Subs will be used to provide you with a choice of how to utilize players that can't handle 90 minutes, while allow for others to get game time. - Injuries and knocks will further ask the question of whether you want to play someone 30 minutes, or maybe rest completely.  Anyhow, I've not thought through all of this deeply, but it's mostly the direction I lean towards if someone were to ask me.

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part5.txt:19233 | [2026-09-03 10:29] derbymanager : The worst average across the 4 primary skills for keepers is 15 in the league. It's hard to differentiate between a player with 20 in handling and 18. Since the range between the worst and best average skill is 5, which amounts to about 13% save rate, and there are 4 skills in that average... That means the difference in handling 19 and 20 is about +/- 0.65% save rate. And that's if skills were the only thing affecting this, and they aren't. There's experience (which, it seems, is quite important), club fit, form, and of course, your tactic and defenders and everything else. I would expect that +1 in handling is maybe at +0.3 or +0.4% increase in save rate.   So the fact that your keeper has everything at 20 isn't really special at all. It's actually the issue with the game, because the keepers are too easy to develop. You need 3-4 primary skills and 1-2 secondary ones and you're done with it. But the game is set up to train outfield players that need 2x that many skills so GKs basically train 2x faster and can reach 2x higher levels. Obviously it's not fun if all keepers are the same and I'm inclined to simply drop all GKs' skills by 30% and slow down training for them so that there would be larger variety between them. Obviously, that would make everyone lose value and people would be unhappy so I probably won't do it...  One other thing. Looking at xgk is maybe ok to evaluate a keeper quickly but it always underrepresents since all shots off target are excluded. It's like trying to measure how many cars crash on the road, but then exclude all cars that didn't crash. Since we excluded shots off target (which also had a chance to end up as goals) and are comparing only shots on target, the goals that a keeper concedes are always higher than xgk. Each shot should be counted even if it was off target because that represents the real challenge the keeper faced. If I miss an empty goal that shouldn't muddy the statistics.

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part6.txt:3137 | [2026-06-20 17:12] furysk : My thoughts on the current system, and in general what i think is good or bad about it:  Good - It has brought the average age of a developing player down from what was basically 17-18 on the transfer list to 16-17.  That extra 30 days of development average for the people to utilize is very important imo in getting more mileage out of developing them, assuming their development age is close to their true age.    Good - the options available to train for lower level teams has expanded significantly.  Teams are less likely to settle on a few players in their school because of the age gap between school and the earliest available TL'd player (which takes a player exitting school or a team buying a guy out of school and TL'ing him at the earliest availability) and because of this more of the 'right guys' have a potential chance to be recruited in.  Bad - For higher level teams, this system is not nearly as helpful.  In some aspects, this design is a good thing, but they become reliant on finding a spot for lets say on average a 1M-1.5M at best prospect in their lineup card that would otherwise have a 10-12m player, meaning the cost of acquisition to them also has to include the potential value of losses incurred due to the fielding of that player, not just the amount they spent to bring them in.  Bad - it's a heavier overall investment cost now to find veteran players on the open market, because we're now dealing with not only lower understanding of veterans skills than when i first started but we are also dealing with a larger range of true valuation on the veteran players.  Bad - This system is reliant on human players not getting attached to a larger percentage of the players they develop, so that they are actually training players for sale value rather than trying to take them from league 4/tier 4 to the top.  I personally see too much wasted wage budget on middle aged guys that have stopped development because they reached the tier max that teams should have sold.
data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part6.txt:3139 | [2026-06-20 17:27] furysk : Heavier scouting investment cost - I think that veterans of the world should have a larger 'book' on them, and should have smaller ranges of skills and of potential values than players who are less experienced.  I would make barely experienced a wide range, somewhat slightly less wide ranged, fairly experienced even less range, and highly experienced should come with very little doubt as to what they can do.  Scouts should have plenty of communication with scouts between regions, and this should allow them to find more information on just basic phone conversations and tapes they can get for free.  Slowing down human players on building their teams is more frustrating than a good thing.
